cohort: The study included 100 viable twin pregnancies beyond 24 weeks gestation and 115 singleton pregnancies as controls from a tertiary care hospital.
finding: Twin pregnancies showed significantly higher rates of maternal, obstetric, and neonatal complications, including preterm labour, PPROM, hypertensive disorders, gestational diabetes, NICU admissions, respiratory distress syndrome, and low birth weight, compared to singleton pregnancies.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates were significantly higher in twin pregnancies (54% vs 38%) mainly due to malpresentation.
birth_weight: Outcome measured included low birth weight (<2500 g).
gest_age: Viable twin pregnancies beyond 24 weeks of gestation were included, and preterm labour was measured as an outcome.
